local.rationale: All three distinctions are deterministic checks over two small in-package artifacts with no authorship or isolation conditions, so a single worker resolves every evidence requirement with admissible evidence, and every evidence record is first-time (novel) worker output.

local-independent-verify.rationale: The examiner will confirm the same rule verdicts, so all requirements are still satisfied (resolution fraction 1.0), but the examiner's records merely re-derive evidence the worker already fully established, making roughly half of all evidence records duplicates.

isolated-child.rationale: No admissibility condition requires a causally separated origin, so the isolated process's audit output duplicates what the worker can fully establish alone; requirements are met but about half the evidence records are redundant re-derivations.

branching.rationale: With no isolation-demanding distinction, the run-time choice should realize the local branch, giving local-family behavior (all requirements satisfied by novel worker evidence) while being costed at the isolated-child rate.
